implementation.mechanism_vs_implementation: nothing of c2rust is absorbed: its crates, indexed by rust-analyzer, exposed the class (calls inside standard macro arguments never reach the resolver); the fix follows the documented expansions of the standard macros (how each argument is evaluated -- by value, through format_args!'s shared reference, compared by reference, autoref'd as write_fmt's receiver) and rustc's MIR for where their temporaries drop, not any c2rust code
implementation.change: adapter semantic::rust::resolve: expand_standard_macros / evaluation (each recovered standard macro becomes the tuple of its evaluated arguments, marked; conditional arguments marked), expanded_macro (the G169 temporaries keep it opaque), conditional (holder analysis enters conditional arguments and the right operand of &&/|| one level deeper), DefMap::collect_crate discovers the crate's files first; adapter semantic::rust::macros::shadowing_macro_names (macro_rules names, use-bound names, #[macro_use] extern crate) replaces local_macro_names for the resolver and every extractor walker
implementation.review: an independent adversarial review of the first version found two holes, each reproduced against rustc 1.90.0's MIR and closed: (H1) a join or drop in an assert! message or any debug_assert! argument was claimed as the holder's release -- it runs only when the assertion fails, or not at all without debug assertions (with the older short-circuit shape `a || h.join().is_ok()`); (H2) a bare dbg!/vec!/println! bound to another macro by `use`, a std rename or another file's macro_rules was expanded as the standard one
